head: f4abd41
method: full read of all 22 changed backend/frontend files plus 11 executable probes run against the built app and shipped modules; every BLOCK reproduced, no source edited

prior_blocks_verified.CR-001-prior: closed - is_finite guard present, 9 parametrized non-finite cases, frontend matches
prior_blocks_verified.CR-002-prior: partly - Div/FloorDiv/math detection genuinely fixed, but the new exemption is over-broad (see CR-003)
prior_blocks_verified.CR-003-prior: closed - pure-ASGI middleware outside ServerErrorMiddleware; 500 echoes X-Request-ID and logs at the real status
prior_blocks_verified.CR-004-prior: closed - uvicorn/uvicorn.error routed through the JSON root handler

findings.title: Frozen non-2xx error envelope applied only to AppError
findings.detail: api-contracts.md:26-29 mandates {error, detail, context} for every non-2xx response and names 401/403/404/409/422 explicitly. register_exception_handlers registers one handler, for AppError. Probe against the shipped app: 404 -> {"detail":"Not Found"}, 405 -> {"detail":"Method Not Allowed"}, 422 -> {"detail":[{...}]}, 500 -> text/plain 'Internal Server Error'. None carries error or context; the 500 is not JSON. GET /nope reproduces this today. E15-S1 owns 'the single error-mapping table' per component-map.md, and E4-S4 reads threshold_kind/configured_value out of context. No test covers any non-AppError status.
findings.fix: Extract the body into one _envelope(error, detail, context) helper and register three more handlers over it: starlette HTTPException (error=type(exc).__name__, detail=exc.detail, context={}), fastapi RequestValidationError (context={'errors': exc.errors()}), and Exception -> 500 {'error':'InternalServerError','detail':'Internal Server Error','context':{}}. Add one test per status asserting all three keys.

findings.title: Registered PII leaks unredacted, with an empty request_id, when the exception carrying it escapes the redact_values scope
findings.detail: redact_values resets _sensitive_values on __exit__ during stack unwinding, and CorrelationIdMiddleware resets request_id_var in its finally. uvicorn.error's 'Exception in ASGI application' line - now routed into the JSON stream by the CR-004 fix - is emitted after both resets. Reproduced: PAN LEAKED: True, with {"logger":"uvicorn.error","request_id":"","exception":"...ValueError: rejected application for pan=ABCDE1234F"}. Breaks E15-S1-AC1 (0 occurrences) and E15-S1-AC3 (100% of lines carry request_id). Reachable: api-contracts.md:145 puts domain values into error detail strings.
findings.fix: (1) Make the sensitive set request-scoped: bind _sensitive_values to a fresh set in CorrelationIdMiddleware and reset it in the same finally as request_id_var, so redact_values adds to a live set without removing on exit. (2) Wrap 'await self.app(...)' in 'except BaseException: _access_logger.exception(...)' and suppress the re-raise once http.response.start has been seen, so uvicorn never renders a second unscrubbed copy. Add a test that lets a PII-bearing exception escape the route and asserts the value absent from and the request id present on every captured line.

findings.title: Per-line money-guard exemption silences every float category, not just division
findings.detail: _exempt_lines is a substring scan and the 'lineno in exempt' check at line 70 short-circuits the float() call, float-literal and math.* tests as well as Div/FloorDiv. Reproduced: 'rate = float(raw)  # money-guard: decimal-division' -> 0; '0.105  # money-guard: decimal-division' -> 0; 'math.floor(y)  # money-guard: decimal-division' -> 0. This file is the E9-S1-AC2/AC3 oracle and the guard every later money story inherits, so a genuine float leak can be hidden behind a comment claiming a Decimal division. test_float_guard_allows_explicitly_marked_decimal_division pins the over-broad behaviour as desired.
findings.fix: Delete the blanket 'if getattr(node, "lineno", None) in exempt: continue' at line 70 and apply the exemption only inside the division branch: 'if is_division and getattr(node, "lineno", None) in exempt: continue'. Add negative tests asserting non-zero counts for float(raw), 0.105 and math.floor(y) each carrying the exemption comment.

findings.title: GET /health body diverges from the frozen contract
findings.detail: Returns {"status":"ok"}; frozen api-contracts.md:315 specifies {"status":"ok","database":"ok","version":"..."}. E15-S1-AC5 only requires 'a JSON body' so no AC fails, but the endpoint contract does. Note the internal conflict: the security posture for an unauthenticated probe argues against disclosing version at all.
findings.fix: Add version from Settings now and record an amendment under specs/design/amendments/ deferring database to E15-S2 (when a DB exists), or take the frozen-contract amendment to a human. api-contracts.md is frozen - reported as a conflict, not edited.

findings.title: GET /metrics, assigned to E15-S1 by the frozen design, is missing with no deferral record
findings.detail: api-contracts.md:38 and architecture.md:257 assign GET /metrics to E15-S1, and reasons-canvas.md:234 lists it in the platform-first operation. It is not implemented. The story's own ACs and Generation Contract Operations omit it, so the sealed story and the frozen design disagree.
findings.fix: Record the deferral (to E15-S3, which owns the SLO ACs) under specs/design/amendments/, or implement it. Do not edit the frozen docs.

findings.title: Money enforces no NUMERIC(14,2) magnitude bound, so it can serialize outside the frozen wire pattern
findings.detail: Reproduced: Money(Decimal('1E+20')) is accepted and _serialize_money emits '100000000000000000000.00' - 21 integer digits. The frozen wire schema is {"type":"string","pattern":"^-?[0-9]{1,12}\\.[0-9]{2}$"} (api-contracts.schema.json:893) and D-G fixes storage at NUMERIC(14,2). Money is the designated single enforcement point for D-G, so the range half of the invariant is enforced nowhere; failure would surface as an unmapped driver error at insert time. No caller exists yet, hence WARN not BLOCK.
findings.fix: In Money.__init__, after quantization, raise InvalidMoneyAmountError when abs(amount) >= Decimal('1E12'). Add boundary tests: 999999999999.99 accepted, 1000000000000.00 rejected.

findings.title: Unvalidated log_level makes a lowercase env value crash the server at import
findings.detail: log_level: str is passed straight to root.setLevel. Reproduced: TRUELEND_LOG_LEVEL=debug -> ValueError: Unknown level: 'debug'; same for '' and any typo. Because app = create_app() runs at module scope, this is an unhandled exception at import of src.api.app - the server refuses to boot on the conventional lowercase spelling uvicorn itself uses (--log-level debug).
findings.fix: Type it Literal['DEBUG','INFO','WARNING','ERROR','CRITICAL'] with a field_validator(mode='before') that upper-cases, so a bad value fails as a readable settings validation error at startup.

findings.title: Sensitive values shorter than 6 characters are silently not redacted
findings.detail: _MIN_REDACTABLE_LENGTH = 6 makes _scrub skip any registered value below that length with no signal to the caller who explicitly marked it sensitive. Reproduced: redact_values('12345') -> '"message": "value=12345"', leaked. AC1's three values are all >= 10 chars so AC1 passes; a short document id or amount marked sensitive by a later story will not be protected. No test covers the short-value path.
findings.fix: Do not skip silently: match short values with \\b word boundaries instead of the separator-tolerant pattern, or raise/logger.warning at redact_values time so the caller learns the value is unprotected. Add a test for the short-value path.

findings.title: RedactionFilter destroys record.args, forcing uvicorn.access to be disabled behind a 7-line apology
findings.detail: filter() sets record.args = () on the shared record, so any formatter reading record.args breaks. That is the stated root cause of the comment at logging.py:143-149 disabling uvicorn.access ('its AccessFormatter reads record.args, which RedactionFilter clears, raising ValueError'). A workaround needing a paragraph of justification signals the code is wrong, and here it is fixable.
findings.fix: Preserve the record shape: scrub the template and each argument separately (record.msg = _scrub(str(record.msg), vals); record.args = tuple(_scrub(str(a), vals) for a in record.args)), reformat uvicorn.access through the JSON formatter instead of disabling it, and delete the apology comment.

findings.title: Access log line carries no latency, and uvicorn.access is disabled, so nothing supports the p95 SLO
findings.detail: The one surviving access line is '%s %s -> %s' (method, path, status) with no duration, and uvicorn.access - the only other per-request timing source - is disabled. Nothing in the log stream supports the project runtime SLO {"p95_ms": 500} or E15-S3-AC1.
findings.fix: Capture time.perf_counter() at scope entry and emit duration_ms on the access line as a formatter field (not string-interpolated), so the SLO sensor has a source.

findings.title: extra= fields silently discarded, and RedactionFilter never scrubs record.__dict__
findings.detail: JSONLogFormatter builds its payload from a fixed key list, so logger.info(..., extra={...}) fields never appear (reproduced: applicant_pan set on the record is absent from the output). Today that is accidentally safe only because RedactionFilter also ignores record.__dict__ - the moment a later story adds extras to the payload they ship unredacted.
findings.fix: Either serialise a whitelisted extra mapping through _scrub in the same change, or assert the limitation with a test so no story can add extras without also adding redaction for them.

findings.title: lru_cache keyed on the raw sensitive value retains PII in process memory past the request scope
findings.detail: _redaction_pattern is @lru_cache(maxsize=256) keyed on the raw value, and the compiled re.Pattern retains it in .pattern. Up to 256 applicant PANs/Aadhaars stay resident indefinitely - the opposite of the module's purpose. Secondary: for salary-document content (an explicit AC1 target) the compiled pattern scales with document size and is re-applied to every log line in scope, against a 500 ms p95 budget.
findings.fix: Key the cache on a hashlib.sha256 digest of the value, or drop the cache and compile per call for values above a size threshold. Disclosure impact is the security-reviewer's call; flagged here as a lifecycle/retention defect.

findings.title: The single classifier's published name, signature and module all differ from the sealed Generation Contract
findings.detail: E11-S1 Operation 2 seals classify(days_past_due: int) -> DelinquencyBucket in backend/src/types/delinquency.py reading floors from config. Shipped: classify_by_days_past_due(int) and classify(date, date) in config/delinquency.py, with types/delinquency.py holding only the enum. The implementation is right - the sealed text would require Types to import Config, which the one-way layering forbids - but E11-S2 and E12-S1 are planned against the sealed signature and no amendment is recorded.
findings.fix: Record the deviation in specs/design/amendments/ naming both shipped signatures so the consuming stories are planned against what exists. Do not edit the frozen component-map or the story's sealed Operations.

findings.title: Frontend float guard has no division pattern and never scans MoneyText.tsx
findings.detail: FLOAT_RISK_PATTERNS contains no division pattern, and countFloatRisks is only run against src/types/money.ts. The backend guard's own docstring names 'principal / months' as the most likely leak; the frontend guard cannot see it. MoneyText.tsx - the other half of the E9-S1 frontend surface, and where AC3's 'carried and formatted' formatting is consumed - is never scanned.
findings.fix: Add a division pattern (e.g. /[^*/\s]\s*\/\s*[A-Za-z_$(\d]/) with a matching positive case in the it.each table, and scan src/ui/components/MoneyText.tsx in the same test.

findings.title: multiply throws a raw decimal.js error, and the frontend non-finite guard has no test
findings.detail: multiply calls new Decimal(scalar) outside any try/catch, so a non-numeric scalar string throws a raw decimal.js Error rather than InvalidMoneyAmountError - inconsistent with fromWire, which wraps it. Separately the non-finite guard at money.ts:31 has no test at all, while the backend has nine parametrized cases for the same rule.
findings.fix: Route the scalar through toQuantizedDecimal (or wrap the construction in the same try/catch), and add expect(() => Money.fromWire('NaN')).toThrow(InvalidMoneyAmountError) plus the 'Infinity' case.

findings.title: Negative zero reaches the wire and the UI as "-0.00"
findings.detail: Reproduced: Money('-0.001') -> Decimal('-0.00'), _serialize_money -> '-0.00', and MoneyText renders '-0.00'. Equality and hashing are correct (Money('-0.001') == Money('0.00') is True), so this is presentation rather than arithmetic - but a balance displayed as '-0.00' is a defect a user will report.
findings.fix: Normalise in _quantize: if quantized.is_zero(): return quantized.copy_abs(). Add the case to the quantization parametrize table.

findings.title: Two tests mutate global logging config with no teardown, making the suite order-dependent
findings.detail: test_uvicorn_loggers_do_not_bypass_json_formatting (line 149) and test_redaction_filter_covers_every_logger_under_the_real_server_config (line 310) both call logging.config.dictConfig(uvicorn LOGGING_CONFIG) then configure_logging(...) and never restore. They leave uvicorn.access permanently disabled and the root handler list replaced for the rest of the session - the exact failure mode that forced log_capture to declare a dependency on client (conftest.py:36).
findings.fix: Wrap both in a fixture that snapshots logging.root.handlers, root.level and the disabled/propagate/handlers state of the touched loggers, and restores them in teardown.

findings.title: AC2's negative control uses an unregistered logger, dodging the real question
findings.detail: E15-S1-AC2 requires that 'a logger registered without it fails the assertion'. The control constructs logging.Logger('unregistered-probe-logger') directly, which is not in logging.root.manager.loggerDict. Any logger created after configure_logging genuinely has no filter (the handler-level filter is what protects those lines), and a registered probe would expose that.
findings.fix: Use logging.getLogger('probe-after-configure') and assert the intended behaviour explicitly - either that _install_redaction_filter_everywhere is re-runnable, or that the handler-level filter is the real control. Note the per-logger loop at logging.py:167 is redundant for every propagating logger.

findings.title: PII-scope control substring-matches 'pan' and exempts any file named logging.py
findings.detail: _modules_referencing_pii substring-matches 'pan'/'aadhaar'/'salary_doc' against the lower-cased whole file. 'pan' matches expand, company, panel, span - so this control will fail on unrelated modules as the codebase grows, and the natural response to a false positive is to weaken it. It also skips any file basenamed logging.py anywhere under src/, so a future src/service/logging.py is silently exempt.
findings.fix: Match with re.search(rf'\\b{field}\\b', lowered), and compare the resolved path against src/config/logging.py rather than module.name.

findings.title: Duplicate error-envelope test
findings.detail: test_app_error_is_mapped_to_a_typed_json_response (line 113) and test_error_envelope_context_defaults_to_empty (line 431) are the same test: both register a throwaway route raising AppError('boom', status_code=418) and both assert {'error':'AppError','detail':'boom','context':{}}.
findings.fix: Delete the one at line 113; the later one carries the clearer name and docstring.

findings.title: 0-byte package marker inconsistent with its own sibling packages, and unowned in the frozen component map
findings.detail: src/api, src/config, src/types and src/api/platform have no __init__.py, so the tree is already an implicit-namespace layout and this single marker is inconsistent with its siblings. It is also the open ownership-check block: no row in the frozen component-map.md.
findings.fix: Delete it and re-run 'uv run pytest -q' and 'uv run mypy src/'. If both stay green that clears the ownership block without amending a frozen artefact or spending a human re-record. If mypy needs it, add the three sibling __init__.py files for consistency and take the map amendment to a human.

findings.title: Module-level app = create_app() reads the environment and mutates global logging on import
findings.detail: Importing src.api.app calls Settings() and root.handlers.clear(). Every build_fastapi_app() call repeats the handler reset, which is why log_capture must depend on client and documents the ordering in a four-line docstring. Import-time side effects also turn CR-007 into a boot failure rather than a startup validation error.
findings.fix: Move configure_logging(settings) out of build_fastapi_app into a FastAPI lifespan startup hook, or make the handler install idempotent, so importing the module has no side effect and fixtures need no ordering trick.

findings.title: The exception-redaction test asserts a state the production path never reaches
findings.detail: test_exception_tracebacks_are_redacted_and_rendered constructs and formats the record inside the 'with redact_values(pan):' block. An exception that reaches the server's logger has by definition unwound out of that block, so the test cannot fail if CR-002 is present. This is the assertion that let CR-002 through.
findings.fix: Move the filt.filter(record) and formatter.format(record) calls outside the with block. That test then fails until CR-002 is fixed, which is the point.

findings.title: Speculative gunicorn.error entry
findings.detail: _JSON_ROUTED_LOGGERS includes 'gunicorn.error'; gunicorn is not a dependency (uvicorn[standard] only), so this routes a logger for a server the project does not run.
findings.fix: Remove 'gunicorn.error' until a story introduces gunicorn.

findings.title: Non-finite guard justified by a claim that is not true of this type
findings.detail: money.py:52 and test_no_float_money.py:159 both justify the guard by claiming 'an ordering comparison against an underwriting threshold raises InvalidOperation'. Money defines no ordering operators, so any comparison raises TypeError (verified). The guard is right; the stated reason is not. Related: E4-S4's threshold checks will need __lt__/__le__, which no story has assigned.
findings.fix: Correct both comments to cite the real consequences (equality with itself is False; the serializer would emit "NaN"), and raise the missing-ordering gap when E4-S4 is planned.

findings.title: Money arithmetic depends on the mutable global decimal context
findings.detail: Verified: with decimal.getcontext().prec = 6, Money('999999.99').multiply(Decimal('1.05')) raises InvalidMoneyAmountError. Any unrelated module that changes the global context silently changes money behaviour. The frontend's decimal.js default precision is 20 significant digits vs Python's 28, so the two sides can also diverge on very large intermediate products.
findings.fix: Wrap add/subtract/multiply in decimal.localcontext() with an explicit prec so money arithmetic is independent of global state, and pin Decimal.set({ precision: 28 }) on the frontend to match.

findings.title: MoneyField rejects int while Money accepts it
findings.detail: _validate_money accepts Money | str | Decimal but rejects int, whereas Money.__init__ accepts int. Verified: Model(amount=1234) raises ValidationError. Harmless, but an inconsistency between the type and its only serializer that will surprise a caller building a model in code.
findings.fix: Add int to the isinstance check in _validate_money (floats remain rejected by Money itself), or document the narrower input set.

findings.title: Unreachable default bucket masks a future table-ordering mistake
findings.detail: bucket = DPD_BUCKET_FLOORS[0][0] can never be read: the first floor is 0 and negatives are rejected above. If the table is ever reordered or its first floor changes, the function silently returns CURRENT instead of failing.
findings.fix: Drop the pre-seed and raise if DPD_BUCKET_FLOORS[0][1] != 0, so a bad table fails loudly.

findings.title: Story scope still names the integer-minor-unit form that D-J forbids
findings.detail: E9-S1 Scope In reads 'Frontend integer-minor-unit money module', which D-J and component-map.md:123-129 explicitly rule out. The shipped code correctly follows D-J. specs/stories/** is an allowed path, so the stale line can be re-rendered; left as-is a later reader may implement the forbidden form.
findings.fix: Re-render the E9-S1 scope line from the D-J-amended AC via /spec, so the story and the design agree.

findings.title: tsconfig includes a vitest.config.ts that does not exist
findings.detail: frontend/vitest.config.ts is named in E9-S1 Operation 4 and listed in tsconfig include, but the file does not exist; the vitest config lives in vite.config.ts. Functionally equivalent.
findings.fix: Remove the dead 'vitest.config.ts' entry from tsconfig include.

findings.title: AC3 is proven over a single access-log line, never over a handler-emitted one
findings.detail: The AC3 test iterates one captured line (truelend.access). No test asserts that a line logged from inside a route handler carries the request id - the actual propagation claim. Verified working for both async def and threadpool def handlers, so this is a coverage gap rather than a defect.
findings.fix: Have the AC3 test route emit one business log line and assert its request_id too.
